title: Kupor teases department-specific Tech Force tracks
summary: The two-year program has so far onboarded about 500 engineers across various agencies.

title: They left federal service and ran for Congress. Even in defeat, they found a new way to serve
summary: At least two former feds will be members of the House next year.

title: Classified NSA communications network down, people familiar say
summary: There aren’t any immediate signs that the outage on NSA Net is related to a cyberattack, and it may be linked to a series of software upgrades on the network.

title: GAO's independence matters more than ever as a new comptroller general is chosen
summary: COMMENTARY | The FAA's nationwide ground stop exposed the consequences of poor agency management. The watchdog that warned of trouble needs a leader committed to its nonpartisan mission.

title: Trump taps OMB deputy to lead GAO amid rushed selection process
summary: Eric Ueland would serve a 15-year term leading the congressional watchdog that has challenged the Trump administration's spending and workforce actions.

title: OPM's plan to make feds sign NDAs faces new challenge on Capitol Hill
summary: New legislation would bar the Trump administration from using federal funds to finalize or implement the Office of Personnel Management’s proposal to require all federal workers to sign a non-disclosure agreement.

title: Federal tech fellows would get an expedited path to permanent jobs under a new bill
summary: While the Trump administration’s Tech Force initiative assigns young tech employees to agencies for two-year tours, the sponsor of a new House measure wants to “open the door” to longer-term service.

title: Hegseth wants to elevate the civilian special-ops chief. Congress may not let him
summary: The assistant defense secretary for special ops would rise to service-secretary level, if lawmakers allow it.

title: Legacy tech issue led to FAA’s nationwide ground stop
summary: The ground stop delayed more than 10,000 flights Friday, though officials said there was no indication of a cyber-attack or relation to the Microsoft outage earlier in the week.

title: CDC director acknowledges employee trust is at an ‘all-time low’
summary: Dr. Erica Schwartz is trying to rebuild trust with a workforce still reeling from staffing cuts and leadership upheaval. But her remarks Thursday included another misidentification of the officer killed at CDC headquarters last year.

title: VA plans further VA.gov updates as it looks to expand AI integration
summary: The department is working with America.gov to shape how AI tools interact with its website, while planning additional modernization releases in the new year.

title: State Department to pilot online passport applications for first-time applicants
summary: The pilot application will be accessible through America.gov, the federal government’s AI-powered chatbot.

title: OPM’s federal hiring push runs up against young workers’ waning interest
summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and OPM Director Scott Kupor urged students at Texas Christian University to consider federal careers despite the administration’s cuts to the workforce.

title: House pushes competing veterans’ benefits bills through in unusual votes
summary: Lawmakers passed a bill ending a provision preventing some combat-wounded veterans from collecting both military retirement pay and veterans’ disability compensation as well as a less generous version of that legislation, coupled with billions in other spending cuts.

title: What retirees should know about health insurance during Open Season
summary: Federal retirement benefits expert Tammy Flanagan and Executive Editor Tanya Ballard Brown discuss what federal employees nearing retirement and current retirees should consider when choosing health coverage during Open Season.

title: Lame-duck Congress expedites search for next GAO leader
summary: The last time lawmakers vetted candidates for GAO’s top job, a congressional commission spent more than a year on its search. Now members are being given 24 hours to find candidates in a process top Democrats call a "sham."

title: VA staffing losses are disrupting critical services at multiple hospitals
summary: At one New Jersey facility, departures left gaps in surgery, wound care and other services. ProPublica found similar disruptions at VA hospitals in three other states.

title: What federal agencies stand to gain by hiring more veterans
summary: COMMENTARY| The IRS has made veteran recruitment a workforce priority. Its chief human capital officer explains why military experience can be an asset across government.

title: Honoring veterans means keeping our promises to them
summary: COMMENTARY | Veterans facing delayed care, disrupted services and long waits for benefits depend on a VA workforce equipped to meet their needs.

title: Feds urge judge to block OPM’s gender affirming care ban
summary: Experts say between 40,000 and 60,000 transgender federal workers have been or will be impacted by the Trump administration's effort to ban coverage of hormone therapies and other gender-affirming treatments.

title: Federal agencies want young talent. They need to rethink the pitch, experts say
summary: Despite the Trump administration’s cuts to the civil service, recruiting more early-career workers into agencies has been a bipartisan priority.

title: USPS ‘got the job done’ delivering ballots, as postal unions push to permanently block mail-in voting EO restrictions
summary: A largely self-funded USPS is asking the incoming Democrat-controlled Congress for substantially more funding as the agency looks to avoid running out of cash.
